title: Async trace adapter migration and LogWriter refactor to reduce allocs & blocking I/O
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our current tracing and logging integration uses a combination of an in-house tracing shim layered on top of OpenTelemetry 1.x and a Logback appender that performs synchronous formatting and remote buffer flushes. Production profiling shows significant per-request allocations and occasional blocking on log append when remote sidecar is under pressure, causing P99 latency spikes. Goal: Replace the legacy tracing shim with the official OpenTelemetry SDK v1.20 idiomatic usage (Context propagation, InstrumentationLibrary, explicit Span processors), and replace the Logback appender with an asynchronous low-allocation LogWriter backed by a lock-free ring buffer and batched sender. This ticket covers the refactor, package upgrades, compatibility shims for existing attribute names, tests, and a phased rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration test coverage for new Otel setup (trace context preserved across async boundaries)
End-to-end smoke: traces from API gateway through runtime show correct span names and attributes for top 10 routes
Logging write path allocations reduced by >= 70% in bench microservice (heap profile comparison)
No increase in error rate after deploying new LogWriter for 24h in canary (error budget unaffected)
Fallback mode: if LogWriter queue is full, logs are dropped to a local disk spool and a metric is emitted (configurable)
Documentation updated: migration notes, config knobs, and runbook
plan: 1) Audit current tracing shim and map all exported attribute keys and resource tags
2) Prototype: implement Otel SDK initialization with BatchSpanProcessor + Resource detection and injection (branch: feat/otel-migrate-48801)
3) Implement compatibility layer to translate legacy attribute keys to new semantic conventions
4) Replace Logback appender with async LogWriter library (in repo under infra/logwriter) using lock-free ring buffer and batch flush; add configurable max queue and spool path
5) Benchmark microservice: compare allocations and latencies vs baseline using bench harness (bench/observability/alloc-test)
6) Canary deploy to runtime-canary (5% traffic) with observability booleans and feature flags for immediate rollback
7) Monitor metrics: span counts, dropped logs, log_queue_length, log_spool_events, request_latency_p99. If stable for 48h, widen rollout
8) Finalize docs, create tech note for on-call, and schedule postmortem follow-up to capture lessons
